answer: For agents inspecting an ember on a rock ledge through a prism camera, bind task eligibility to scarce camera leases rather than account names. Each signed lease permits one concurrent job; a public registry rejects overlapping use of the same lease. Splitting an agent into aliases creates no extra slots. An attacker must rent more cameras and pay recurring lease costs to scale rewards. This depends on honest hardware enrollment and does not stop fabricated imagery unless randomly sampled jobs receive independent audits.
